meaning: The number 242 has no well-established symbolic meaning in biblical or Jewish tradition, but appears as a concrete figure in Nehemiah.
description: 242 is not a number that is particularly highlighted in the Bible or in classical Jewish numerology (gematria) with an acknowledged symbolic meaning. Although gematria can link various Hebrew words to the numerical value 242, there is no broad tradition that assigns this number a specific spiritual or symbolic role. The number does appear, however, in Nehemiah 11:13, where 242 brothers are mentioned as heads of priestly families in Jerusalem after returning from the Babylonian exile. Beyond this concrete occurrence, it is not among the numbers that have traditionally held prominent significance in biblical numerology, such as 7, 12, 40 or 613.

footnotes.text: In Nehemiah 11:13, 242 brothers are mentioned who were heads of priestly families. The context is the rebuilding of Jerusalem after the Babylonian exile, where lists of those who settled in the city served as documentation of the restored cultic order.

footnotes.text: In Nehemiah 11:13, 242 brothers are mentioned who were heads of priestly families under the line of Immer (through Amashsai, son of Azarel, son of Azaiah, son of Meshillemoth, son of Immer). The context is the rebuilding of Jerusalem after the Babylonian exile, where lists of those who settled in the city served as documentation of the restored cultic order.
